core.title: Import the test harness from the declared runner
core.given: A test file — any file matching the profile's test-file name patterns, whatever its language or its test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or otherwise) — in a stack whose profile declares the test runner and its harness
core.when: the test file is written or changed
core.then: Import the test harness from the declared runner's own harness module; never import a foreign harness (one that binds the test to a different runner).
prefer: Import the harness — the test API the file uses — from the declared runner's own harness module.
Run the tests with the declared runner's own test command.
avoid: Importing the harness from a foreign module — the test is not run by the declared runner.
Expecting a test kept on a foreign harness during a migration to be exempt: it stays reported until it moves; the finding is the migration's explicit, reviewable open item.
Toolchain sprawl: a foreign harness drags its own runner and transform pipeline back into the toolchain.
unless: The file is not a test file (a harness import outside a test file is a different smell, not scanned).
core.why: The obligation is strict because the ATDD cost exceeds sprawl: acceptance tests are the evidence a phase gate consumes, reported in terms of its declared runner; a test bound to a foreign harness is coverage the gate believes ran but never did — a green gate with an unexercised acceptance. A test the gate cannot run is worse than no test.
evidence: No test file imports or requires a foreign harness; harness imports come from the declared runner's harness module.
The declared runner executes the acceptance tests, and this rule's harness-discipline check reports zero findings.
verification: Checks test files only: a file matching the profile's test-file name patterns is scanned whatever its language or its test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or otherwise); non-test files are never scanned (a harness import outside a test file is a different smell).
Masks line comments only (the profile's line-comment marker) so a migration note naming the old harness does not trip the check; no other comment form is required to be masked.
Masking never erases harness identifiers inside import expressions — the matched harness name must stay visible however the stack's import syntax represents it.
Flags any import or require of a foreign harness, per the profile's foreign-harness list: frameworks that drag their own runner and transform pipeline back in.
The declared runner is the one the stack's profile declares; it is what the binding plan resolves and what the phase gate reports as having executed.
No per-rule exemption: a test deliberately retained on a foreign harness during a migration stays reported until it moves.
Disposition strict, severity 2: every finding fails.

fires: A test file matching the profile's test-file name patterns — whatever its language or its test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or otherwise) — in a stack that declares the runner is created or edited (the harness must come from the declared runner's harness module).
A test file imports its test API from a foreign harness module.
A test file imports or requires a foreign harness package — module usage inside the test file is the trigger, not a mere dependency declaration.
A test kept on a foreign harness during a migration is still in the tree.
doesNotFire: A non-test source file imports a foreign harness (a different smell, not scanned).
A test file in a repository governed by a different stack profile (that stack's own realization of this core applies).

profileRequirements.meaning: The runner the stack declares as the one that executes the tests — what the binding plan resolves, what the phase gate reports coverage in terms of, and whose own test command runs the acceptance tests.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the `runtime.runner` provided by capability `atdd.workspace.bun` — `bun`; tests run via `bun test`

profileRequirements.meaning: The import specifier of the declared runner's own test harness — the module every test file must import its test API from.
Import specifiers / package names of foreign harnesses — test frameworks that bind a test to their own runner and transform pipeline instead of the declared runner.
File-name patterns that classify a file as a test file by filename alone — the only files scanned, whatever their language or their test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or other).
profileRequirements.bunValue: `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*` — the detector scans exactly these globs, whatever the file's language; ATDD-Bun does not separate unit, acceptance or e2e test files by name

profileRequirements.meaning: The line-comment syntax whose comments the check masks (line comments only) so a migration note naming the old harness does not trip it.
profileRequirements.bunValue: line comments (`//`) — bun.json verifier_detail[1]: "Masks line comments"

proposedKeys.meaning: File-name patterns that make a file a test file by filename alone, regardless of test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or other) or language.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The suffix group enumerates test kinds only by role (unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test); this rule's scope is every file matching the test-file patterns independent of role — reusing the role-scoped keys would drop e2e and otherwise-classified test files.

proposedKeys.meaning: The import specifier of the declared runner's built-in test harness — the module test files must import their test API from.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: tooling.test_runner names the runner, not the import specifier of its harness; no idiom key says which harness module is the right one.

proposedKeys.meaning: Import specifiers / package names of foreign harnesses — test frameworks bound to their own runner and transform pipeline.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports scopes inner-role imports of runtime machinery and tooling.lockfile.foreign is only about lockfiles; no key lists foreign test harnesses.

bunOnly.text: file_kind = `bun_workspace_member`: file belongs to a Bun stack — workspace provider capability `atdd.workspace.bun` with declared `runtime.runner` = `bun`; observability `needs_new_observer` (a workspace-capability observer).
bunOnly.reason: How ATDD-Bun observes that a file belongs to a stack with a declared runner; the core needs only the declared runner itself (tooling.test_runner) — each stack detects stack membership its own way, so there is no stack-neutral fact of this shape.

bunOnly.text: Zero-dependency Bun detector; scans TEST FILES ONLY (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`).
bunOnly.reason: The detector implementation ('zero-dependency Bun detector') and its hardcoded globs are realization details; the neutral scope — every file matching the profile's test-file patterns, whatever its language or category — is in core verification, with the patterns from suffix.test.

bunOnly.text: Does NOT mask string literals: the harness name lives inside the import's own string literal, so masking literals would blank the very thing being matched.
bunOnly.reason: This prohibition and its rationale are specific to this stack's import syntax, where the module specifier is a string literal; other languages carry module names in imports differently. The stack-neutral requirement is only that masking never erases harness identifiers inside import expressions (core verification); the string-literal rule is the Bun realization of that requirement.

bunOnly.text: `bun test` executes the acceptance tests and the `bun_tester_discipline_detector` reports zero findings.
bunOnly.reason: The detector/validator id of this rule is a realization detail (it has no stack-neutral equivalent); core verification names the check generically, and the runner command comes from tooling.test_runner.

bunOnly.text: Jest-compatible assertions, so usually only the import line changes (with the concrete import `import { describe, expect, it } from "bun:test";`).
bunOnly.reason: Assertion compatibility is a property of this stack's harness pair — bun:test versus the Jest-family harnesses it replaces — not a stack-neutral fact; the core only directs the import to the declared runner's harness, without the compatibility claim.

bunOnly.text: A toolchain premised on Bun running TypeScript directly.
bunOnly.reason: The premise that the declared runner executes the stack's sources directly (no separate compile or transform step) is a Bun/TypeScript toolchain characteristic, not a property of declared runners in general; the core keeps only the general toolchain-sprawl warning.

classification.note: Test-file scope is every file matching the profile's test-file patterns (suffix.test), whatever its language or category — the Bun filename-only scope; the runner comes from tooling.test_runner.
Already stack-neutral.

Rationale already stack-neutral; 'strict' is echoed in core verification.

'Run tests with `bun test`' generalized to the declared runner's own test command.
Neutral form: importing the harness from a foreign module. The concrete `vitest` example is not repeated (rule 4).
Already neutral: no migration exemption; mirrored as the no-per-rule-exemption verification entry.
General toolchain-sprawl warning is neutral; the 'Bun running TypeScript directly' premise is bunOnly.
The single exclusion is both the core's unless and the check's scan scope.
Neutral form; test-file patterns, foreign names and harness module come from the profile.
`bun test` is the profile's runner command; the detector id is bunOnly (rule 7).
Scan scope is neutral verification; globs from suffix.test; detector implementation is bunOnly.

Masking LINE comments only (not block comments or other forms) so a migration note does not trip the check; the line-comment syntax comes from idiom.comment_marker. Narrowed to line comments to match bun.json exactly.
Neutral requirement — masking never erases harness identifiers inside import expressions — is core verification; the string-literal prohibition tied to this stack's import syntax is bunOnly.
Flagging any import or require of a foreign harness is neutral; the five names are the profile list.
Declared runner = what the binding plan resolves and the gate reports; the Bun declaration mechanism is the profile value.
No per-rule exemption for migration tests.
Strict disposition, severity 2 — per-rule, so core verification.
Path globs are the profile's test-file patterns; neutrally file_kind = test.
Test-file classification by filename — same neutral fact as facts[0].
Core needs only 'the stack declares the runner'; the Bun membership fact and its observer are bunOnly.

neutralityNotes: The obligation — every test file imports its harness from the declared runner's own harness module, never a foreign one — is fully neutral; the harness module, foreign-harness list, declared runner, test-file patterns and line-comment syntax come from the profile. Verification masks line comments only (idiom.comment_marker), matching bun.json's 'Masks line comments' exactly — block comments are not required to be masked. Three keys proposed: suffix.test, tooling.test_harness, tooling.foreign_test_harnesses. Residual Bun-specifics in bunOnly: the bun_workspace_member membership fact and its observer; the zero-dependency Bun detector and the bun_tester_discipline_detector id; the Jest-compatibility claim of prefer[0]; the 'Bun running TypeScript directly' premise of avoid[2]; and the no-string-literal-masking rule of verifier_detail[2], whose neutral counterpart is that masking never erases harness identifiers in import expressions. Concrete import examples are not repeated in the core because bun.json ships as the worked reference example.
